note: A Dorian solo that climbs through three positions and comes back down, aiming at {{6}} over the 4th chord the whole way. The positions are now on a position-neck beside the solo-over, so the text names no fret and no crossing string; the chords are tokens counted the long way once, the key is moves (any key) and named only as {{=key}}, and the last line says what stays the same in another key.

exercise.title: Climb through three positions
exercise.why: The 6th of Dorian is the 3rd of the 4th chord and sits in every position, so a solo can move up the neck and still land on it each time that chord comes round.

cells.text:
The backing track loops two chords of {{=key}} Dorian. {{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}, and its 3rd is {{6}}, the note that makes the mode Dorian.
Press Play below to start the backing track. Under it is the neck with positions 1, 2 and 3 of the {{=key}} Dorian scale framed, {{1}} and {{6}} ringed. Start in position 1 and move up a position every few bars, sliding along a string into the next one, until you are in position 3. Land on a ringed {{6}} each time {{chord:IV7}} comes round, wherever you are.
Practice until you find {{6}} before the chord changes, in every position.

Press Play below to start the backing track on {{chord:i7}} and {{chord:IV7}} again, now with drums, bass and keys. Start in position 3 and come down a position every few bars. End your last phrase on the lowest ringed {{1}}.
{{?key}}In another key the three positions sit on other frets, and {{6}} keeps its place inside each one.
